title: The AI-datacenter nuclear buildout - hyperscaler reactor restarts, SMR-developer stakes, and the power-side vendor-financing loop
source: Public record + deal trackers (Data Center Frontier, Constellation/Microsoft, Amazon/X-energy, Google/Kairos, Meta/TerraPower+Oklo+Constellation, SEC filings, NRC, FERC), 2024-2026: every major AI hyperscaler has signed at least one nuclear power agreement for datacenter load; trackers count ~13 announced projects totaling >9.8 GW - the largest corporate nuclear-procurement wave on record. Microsoft: 20yr, ~$16B PPA with Constellation to RESTART Three Mile Island Unit 1 (835 MW, rebranded Crane Clean Energy Center), FERC transmission waiver approved Jun 1 2026, first power targeted H2 2027 - the single most-advanced deal. Amazon: invested ~$700M in X-energy (up to 12 Xe-100 HTGRs) AND an AWS datacenter campus beside Talen Energy's Susquehanna plant (PA) buying up to 1,920 MW via the grid (since Apr 2026, through 2042) - after FERC rejected the original behind-the-meter interconnection-service-agreement amendment (Nov 2024). Google: master agreement with Kairos Power - 50 MW demo scaling to ~500 MW by 2030 (KP-FHR reactors). Meta: the largest commitment - TerraPower (8 Natrium plants, ~2.8 GW) + Oklo (~1.2 GW Aurora campus) + a 20yr PPA for ~1,121 MW from the Clinton plant. Oracle: a 1 GW datacenter design powered by 3 SMRs (permits secured). Sam Altman was Oklo's chairman (via the AltC SPAC) and stepped down Apr 2025 to clear a path for potential OpenAI-Oklo dealings. HONESTY/GRADE: the deals, capacities, PPA terms, the $700M X-energy stake, and the FERC actions are FACT (filings + reporting); the CIRCULARITY read (hyperscalers taking EQUITY in the reactor builders they will then buy power from - a power-side analogue of the chip vendor-financing loop) applies to the EQUITY-STAKE subset (Amazon/X-energy; the Altman/Oklo chairmanship), NOT to the pure PPAs, and is labeled interpretation. CRITICAL CAVEAT (fact): NO datacenter anywhere yet runs on a new reactor built for it - the first new capacity online will be the TMI restart in H2 2027; the SMR fleet deals deliver ~2030-2035, and NuScale's earlier UAMPS/CFPP SMR project was CANCELED in 2023 on cost - so the buildout is largely COMMITMENTS, not delivered power. Overlay/structural edges only (dollar/PPA terms in notes); new SMR-developer nodes are supply-side and do not perturb the AI-financial SCC (unchanged). Companion to energy-power (the buyer-side PPA summary), macro-ai-power-grid-bottleneck, spec-datacenter-ratepayer-costshift.

edges.notes: 20yr ~$16B PPA to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 (835 MW, 'Crane Clean Energy Center'); FERC transmission waiver approved Jun 1 2026; first power H2 2027 - the most-advanced deal and the FIRST new nuclear capacity that will actually serve datacenter load (fact).

Amazon invested ~$700M in X-energy (up to 12 Xe-100 high-temperature gas reactors) - the CLEAREST power-side vendor-financing loop: the hyperscaler takes EQUITY in the reactor developer AND is the offtaker (fact of the stake + offtake; the circular-loop read is labeled interpretation, analogous to the chip vendor-financing in fin-nvidia-openai).

AWS bought a datacenter campus beside Talen's Susquehanna nuclear plant (PA) - a ~$20B+ AI campus - and buys up to 1,920 MW via the grid through 2042; FERC REJECTED the original behind-the-meter interconnection-service-agreement amendment (Nov 2024), forcing the grid-delivered structure - a concrete datacenter-vs-ratepayer grid-cost-allocation wrinkle (fact; cross-ref spec-datacenter-ratepayer-costshift).

Master agreement with Kairos Power: a 50 MW demonstration scaling to ~500 MW by 2030 (KP-FHR molten-salt reactors) - the first corporate next-gen-SMR fleet deal; delivery ~2030 (fact; the timeline is the caveat).
Part of Meta's buildout (the largest hyperscaler commitment, up to ~6.6 GW): TerraPower Natrium (sodium-cooled) - ~8 plants, ~2.8 GW; Bill-Gates-backed (fact; delivery ~2030s).
Meta's ~1.2 GW Oklo Aurora (fast-reactor, HALEU) campus commitment (fact; delivery late-2020s/2030s).
20yr PPA for ~1,121 MW from the Clinton (IL) nuclear plant - backing datacenter load with an EXISTING reactor (nearer-term than the new-build SMRs) (fact).

Altman was Oklo's chairman (taken public via his AltC SPAC) and STEPPED DOWN as chairman Apr 2025 to clear a path for potential OpenAI-Oklo dealings - a governance/circularity tie (OpenAI's power demand <-> an Altman-chaired reactor developer). FACT of the chairmanship + resignation; the OpenAI-offtake intent is labeled (structural, not asserted).
Oracle disclosed a 1 GW datacenter design powered by 3 SMRs with permits secured - a commitment/design, not operating capacity (fact; caveat timeline).

The Xe-100 (like most advanced SMRs) needs HALEU (high-assay low-enriched uranium) - a severe US supply bottleneck largely sourced from Russia historically; the enrichment constraint is a gating risk for the whole SMR fleet (fact of the fuel dependency; cross-ref the HALEU chokepoint).

NuScale has the first NRC-certified SMR design - BUT its flagship UAMPS/Carbon Free Power Project was CANCELED in 2023 on cost overruns, the cautionary counterpoint to the hyperscaler-SMR hype: certification is not delivery, and SMR economics remain unproven at scale (fact).

The thesis: SMRs + reactor restarts power the AI datacenter buildout (~13 projects, >9.8 GW committed). CRITICAL CAVEAT (fact): NO datacenter yet runs on a new reactor built for it; the first new capacity is the TMI restart (H2 2027) and most SMR deliveries are ~2030-2035 - the buildout is COMMITMENTS, not delivered power.
